newsitem.title: FRANCE: French temp agency shares to trade next week.
newsitem.headline: French temp agency shares to trade next week.

text.p: Shares of French temporary help agency Bis SA should start trading again next Tuesday after being suspended this week following the death of company chairman Laurent Negro, a company official said on Thursday.
"It will likely be Tuesday," the official told Reuters by telephone when asked when trading in the stock would resume.

Trading in Bis was halted last Monday at 533 francs ($102) a share in the wake of the death of Negro who founded the company, ranked third in terms of market share in France, and traders expect strong interest when it resumes.

The death of Negro, who pioneered temporary help services in France, has renewed market talk that the family-controlled firm could be the target of a takeover bid by a large foreign temporary help company.
A wave of consolidation has been taking place in the personnel sector, highlighted last year by the merger of Ecco of France and Switzerland's Adia.
The firm has appointed board member Claude Charbonniaud to succeed Negro and said he "will direct the group continuing the policies defined" by Negro last year.
That means, the Bis official said, Bis would continue to seek an international partner. "This is an integral part (of our strategy)," he said. "It will followed in the same fashion."

Last June, Negro said Bis had to take part in the globalisation of personnel services and announced the firm was seeking an international alliance "to satisfy multinational clients who reproach us for not being in New York or Tokyo".
Bis's activities are regarded by financial analysts as being too focused on France.
Possible contenders for Bis, ranking behind Adecco and Manpower, are Netherlands' Randstad Holding NV and Vendex International NV and the U.S. Olsten Corp.

U.S. giant Manpower Inc, known to favour internal growth and outright acquisitions, is reported to have ruled itself out of the running for Bis. Adeco is seen an unlikely contender as it is still digesting the merger that spawned the company.
Negro and his family held some 60 percent of the company which has 4,800 employees and a network of 500 agencies.
Bis, whose market capitalisation totals 2.5 billion francs, posted a first-half profit of 34 million francs, down from 70 million a year earlier.

It forecast 1996 full-year results would be sharply below the previous year's profit of 201 million francs, due to poor trading conditions and a one-off gain that boosted the 1995 results. ($ = 5.214 French Francs)
